correctness.rationale: The genus-three plane quartic is smooth by its exact partial derivatives. Its unique Y=0 point and exhaustive affine fourth-root counts over F9, F81, F729 are verified using irreducible polynomial models and two distinct enumeration orders. Newton identities and Weil functional equation reconstruct the factor (1-3T+9T^2)^3. Semisimple Frobenius satisfies U^2-3U+9, which modulo 7 has roots 1 and 2 with 1-eigenspace dimension 3; the Jacobian order 343 gives rational group (Z/7)^3. No extrapolation from finite samples is used; all fields of the three required extension degrees are exhaustively enumerated.

value.rationale: The 2026 unique one-point classification canonically singles out a genus-three arithmetic curve; unlike its known single base-field point, the complete zeta numerator and full rational Jacobian group are structural invariants encoding all extension-field point counts and the arithmetic isogeny class. The exact group identifies rational 7-torsion rank; it is not a renamed base-field count nor a random unmotivated example. The scope is expressly limited to F9 and no downstream theorem is asserted.
